primary: Machine-learning researchers from subfields other than LLM agents / software-engineering agents: they know general ML, deep learning, standard evaluation practice, and statistics, but not this project's subfield-specific terminology, datasets, or prior work.
secondary: Reviewers/replicators checking whether the reported numbers and comparisons are used honestly and traceably to the source paper.
tertiary: Future readers or practitioners from other subfields who encounter this write-up as an entry point into agent-platform research.
assumed_known: supervised/instruction-tuned large language models (GPT-4, Claude, etc.)
prompting and zero-/few-shot inference in the general in-context-learning sense
standard statistics: percentages, means, comparison against baselines
the general notion of an 'AI agent' that takes actions in an environment (e.g. from reinforcement learning), without subfield-specific tooling
general software engineering vocabulary (a bug, a function, a repository) at a layperson-technical level
not_assumed: SWE-Bench, HumanEvalFix, WebArena, MiniWoB++, GAIA, GPQA, AgentBench, MINT, ProofWriter, Entity Deduction Arena, or what any of them specifically measures
resolve rate / pass@k as SWE-Bench-family-specific metrics
CodeAct-style code-execution action spaces vs. fixed JSON tool-calling
sandboxed/containerized execution as a safety mechanism
the landscape of prior agent frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, MetaGPT, GPTSwarm, BrowserGym, DSPy, SWE-Agent, AutoCodeRover, etc.)
